findings.title: Today's PHP security release, and how we're strengthening PHP security
findings.summary_md: The PHP Foundation published emergency releases fixing CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two unauthenticated remote code execution flaws in the PHP engine collectively known as PHP2Shell. The fixes ship in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 and address memory corruption during request handling and OOM error processing. The advisory recommends immediate patching of all PHP installations serving web requests.

findings.title: Limited reports of PHP bug exploitation emerge
findings.summary_md: GreyNoise reported at least six successful exploitations of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in the days after the flaws were added to the CISA KEV catalog. Dream researchers described a suspected China-nexus campaign chaining PHP2Shell with CVE-2026-46300 against internet-facing firewalls in the US, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, with most activity between October 23 and 24. The report documents roughly 24 compromised firewalls and use of FOFA for target discovery.

findings.title: PayCloud Holdings notice: unauthorized access to Arara Message (first report)
findings.summary_md: PayCloud Holdings' first disclosure reported unauthorized access to subsidiary Arara's email distribution service, with about 3.01 million email addresses taken from one shared system and a web server vulnerability cited as the cause. Arara reported the incident to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission and police, and reconnaissance is described as beginning October 27 with unauthorized logins on October 28. The service was suspended on October 31 pending investigation.

findings.title: PayCloud Holdings notice: unauthorized access to Arara Message (second report)
findings.summary_md: PayCloud's second disclosure revised the impact to approximately 77 million email addresses across roughly 380 client companies after the intrusion spread to additional servers. The report states that about 7.13 million phishing emails impersonating a credit card company were sent from compromised Arara infrastructure between October 28 and 30. The service stores no credit card numbers, and Arara invalidated stolen API keys and administrative passwords.

findings.title: Email Service Breach Leaks 77 Million Addresses, Sparks Phishing Wave
findings.summary_md: CyberNetSec reported that the Arara Message email distribution service, owned by Paycloud Holdings, suffered a breach exposing 77 million email addresses and affecting about 380 corporate clients. The article describes a follow-on phishing campaign of 7.13 million emails impersonating a credit card company and frames the incident as a supply-chain exposure for downstream customers.

findings.title: Arara: Approximately 77 Million Email Addresses Leaked
findings.summary_md: ASCII.jp reported that Arara disclosed approximately 77 million exfiltrated email addresses from its Arara Message service, affecting up to about 380 client companies and 97 servers. The shared-environment count was revised to 3,386,187 addresses across 61 companies, including 411,827 records with names, and about 7.13 million phishing emails were sent between October 28 and 30.
